title: SilkSurf measurement provenance envelope
description: Host, toolchain, and revision facts a measurement depends on. scripts/measurement_environment.py capture() produces exactly this object, and every artifact the repository publishes as evidence embeds one under the key `measurement_environment`. docs/design/CACHE-LOCALITY-CONTRACT.md states the requirement the envelope satisfies: a retained record names the commit, build profile, cache topology, governor, affinity, competing load, and command. A field is null when the host does not expose it rather than absent, so a reader distinguishes an unavailable fact from an unrecorded one.

schema_version.description: Envelope schema generation. A field addition keeps the version; a rename or a semantic change raises it.

timestamp_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the envelope was captured, ending in Z.

git.description: Revision identity of the tree the measurement ran against. Null when the capture runs outside a git checkout.

commit.description: Full 40-character commit SHA, or null when git cannot resolve HEAD.

branch.description: Current branch name, or null on a detached HEAD.

dirty.description: True when the working tree carries uncommitted changes. A dirty record does not reproduce from its commit alone.

toolchain.description: Compiler that built the measured artifact. A rate without a compiler cannot separate an engine change from a codegen change.

rustc.description: Resolved rustc version, the second field of `rustc --version`. Null when rustc is absent from PATH.

rustc_verbose.description: Full `rustc --version` line, which carries the commit hash and release date.

host.description: Machine the measurement ran on. Every field is descriptive evidence; none is a portable threshold.

cpu_model.description: The `model name` field of /proc/cpuinfo. Null off Linux.

logical_cpus.description: Logical CPUs the operating system reports, hardware threads included.

process_affinity.description: Logical CPUs the capturing process may run on. A narrower set than logical_cpus reduces the cache share the workload receives.

load_average.description: One, five, and fifteen minute load averages. Competing load at capture time bounds how much of the machine the measurement had.

cpu_governors.description: Distinct cpufreq scaling governors across all CPUs, sorted. A powersave governor changes latency without changing code.

perf_event_paranoid.description: /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid. The value decides which hardware counters an unprivileged perf run may read.

cache_topology.description: CPU 0 cache descriptors from sysfs, deepest level last. Empty off Linux.

size_bytes.description: Capacity of one instance at this level.

last_level_cache_bytes.description: Largest cache at the deepest data-carrying level. sysfs reports one instance's nominal capacity, so this is an upper bound: affinity, cache sharing, explicit partitions, virtualization, and competing load all reduce the share a workload receives. perf/locality-budget.json treats capacity as a runtime input on these grounds.

environment.description: Recorded environment variables that change what a run measures rather than where it runs. Absent keys were unset.
